result:
The spec's requirements become outcome candidates below. Nothing is ranked yet, because that ranking is yours. No roadmap text has been written.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A filing-index catalog in Parquet for **one real archived quarter**, with each row traceable to its source file | R1, R3 | Small: one `master.idx` download and one parse. The file size is unknown until fetched (see the probe below). |
| O2 | The **full historical baseline** over a range you choose, with a report of every quarter that is complete, pending or failed | R1 | Indexes start at 1993 Q1, so up to about 136 quarters. Request count is trivial: about 136 files plus listings at 3 req/s is a few minutes. Data volume is probably several GB. That figure is extrapolated from a guessed per-quarter size; the probe will firm it up. Your time goes into golden fixtures for every historical format in the range (§4.6), and that grows with how far back you start. |
| O3 | **Daily indexes added on an ongoing basis**, catching up after missed runs, including across quarter boundaries | R2 | One small file per business day, about 250 a year. Catch-up costs little. |
| O4 | **Reprocessing stored inputs** after a parser change, with no new SEC download | R6 | Local compute only. Measured when first run. |
| O5 | **Weekly reconciliation** that picks up SEC corrections to past quarters. Removals wait for your hash-bound approval. | R7, R10 | Material. Each run re-reads every supported quarter, so it moves roughly O2's volume every week. Your time also goes into reviewing withdrawal approvals, at a frequency only running it can tell. |
| O6 | **One shared SEC request budget** across backfill, daily runs and reconciliation | R8 | No direct cost. Set at 3 req/s against SEC's 10 req/s ceiling. |
| O7 | **Readers only ever see complete quarter datasets**, through one active pointer per quarter | R9 | Negligible. |
| O8 | The whole thing **running unattended on Azure**: ADF schedules, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage | R4 | Azure spend is unknown until something is deployed. That track's core stage measures it. |
| O9 | **Run reports and alerts** that show gaps, quarantines, pending approvals and stale discovery | §4.7 | Log Analytics ingestion is part of O8's unknown. |

R5 (one shared implementation) and R11 (stated defaults) describe how the system is built, not what you get, so I've recorded them below as choices.

## Proposed tracks

- **Track A: Catalog** (O1–O7), *known progression*. Spec §2.1 and §7 already name the order: one quarter, then baseline, then daily, then reconciliation.
- **Track B: Azure operation** (O8–O9), *known progression*, ending at the trigger-enablement and scheduled-run evidence in §7 steps 6–9.
  - **Why split:** A answers "is the catalog correct on real SEC data?" and B answers "does it run unattended in production?" Joined, the first real quarter would wait on ADF, identities and infrastructure-as-code. B does depend on A's code, so it can't start first.

If either track feels open to you rather than nameable from first to last, say so and I'll treat it as research.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, uv workspace (repo files)
- Azure services per the ADR. Note the ADR and spec are both still *Proposed*, and §7 step 1 makes their acceptance the first step.
- One shared downloader, parser and publisher for every source (R5)
- The defaults in §4.8 as starting values (R11)
- No SEC downloads in CI (§6)

## Proposed name

`specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. The rule is to use the spec's stem whole.

## Optional probe

I can fetch one real quarter's `master.idx` and one daily `index.json` listing to firm up the O2 and O5 volume notes. I'll only do this if you say yes. It needs the SEC User-Agent identity (organization or name plus contact email) you want to use.

**Your call:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the two tracks against each other. Also confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name, and tell me whether to run the probe.
